title: A guessed --selector misses — pick from candidates in the result, press by --ref
symptom: web click · type end with selector_not_found · element_not_actionable or web_action_failed ('Timeout … exceeded … waiting for locator'). The same failure repeats as selectors are swapped
cause: The selector was guessed without reading the screen. No element matches, or it exists but is hidden or covered, so the target wait (--timeout; 4 s by default for actions, formerly 10 s) runs out. A disabled element ends at once with element_disabled
fix: Pick the right one from candidates in the failure result and call again with --ref as next says (earlier entries are closer to the guessed selector)
launch_cli.py web click --ref <number> --expect-url <part of the new URL>
If there are no candidates, pick with web find --text <button text>
For inputs, get a ref with web inspect --role input and enter it with web type --ref <number> --text <value>
If disabled is true in find · inspect · candidates, or element_disabled comes back, first meet the condition that enables the button (required fields · checkboxes)
If the screen is clearly slow to render, raise it, e.g. --timeout 10
